primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease secondary to diabetic nephropathy

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg PO once daily; increase by 1.25‑2.5 mg every 2 weeks to target BP <130/80 mmHg, max 10 mg daily
medications.duration: Titrate over 4‑6 weeks, then lifelong—review annually
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension and advises monitoring creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 states all CKD patients should receive a statin for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 200 mg PO three times daily with food
medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >20% (approximately 3 months), then reassess
medications.purpose: Treat iron deficiency contributing to anaemia of CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG107/NG203 recommend iron supplementation when ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20% before ESA use

contraindications.reason: eGFR 7.1 mL/min/1.73m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue metformin; consider insulin if glycaemic control needed

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 4 – accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain; avoid nephrotoxic NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Use either an ACE‑I (ramipril) OR an ARB (losartan) but not both

contraindications.reason: eGFR 7.1 mL/min/1.73m² – high risk of hyperkalaemia, especially with ACE‑I
contraindications.alternative: Avoid potassium supplements; monitor serum K+

contraindications.reason: Guideline indication requires eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73m²; patient eGFR 7 is below threshold
contraindications.alternative: Not indicated; focus on ACE‑I, blood pressure control, and dialysis planning

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assume uncontrolled and plan titration of ramipril to target <130/80 mmHg.
Serum potassium level not available – baseline K+ should be measured before starting ramipril and monitored 1‑2 weeks after dose changes.
Liver function tests not available – obtain baseline ALT/AST before initiating atorvastatin.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – oral iron started empirically; will stop or switch to IV iron if ferritin >200 µg/L or TSAT >20%.
Phosphate, calcium, PTH, bicarbonate values not provided – phosphate binders, vitamin D analogues, or sodium bicarbonate will be considered once labs are available.
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or iron allergy before prescribing.
Opioid use disorder not addressed pharmacologically – patient should be referred to addiction services for appropriate management.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril for renoprotection and BP control, atorvastatin for cardiovascular risk reduction, and oral ferrous sulphate to correct iron deficiency anaemia while awaiting iron studies. Avoid metformin, chronic NSAIDs, ACE‑I/ARB combination, high‑dose potassium, and SGLT2 inhibitors due to advanced CKD. Monitor BP, serum creatinine, potassium, liver enzymes, and iron parameters at recommended intervals. Provide non‑pharmacologic advice on smoking cessation, low‑salt diet, weight management, and referral for transplant evaluation, pain management, and addiction support.
